question: What must a driver do to prevent trailers from rolling over when pulling doubles or triples?
choice_a: Keep the heaviest trailer in the last position
choice_b: Maintain highway speed through all curves to reduce time exposed to the turn
choice_c: Steer gently and go slowly around corners, on ramps, off ramps, and curves
choice_d: Use only the trailer hand valve when turning
explanation: To prevent trailers from rolling over, a driver must steer gently and go slowly around corners, on ramps, off ramps, and curves; a safe speed for a single trailer combination may be too fast for doubles or triples.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.1, Prevent Trailer from Rolling Over

question: In a combination of doubles or triples, which trailer is most likely to turn over due to the crack-the-whip effect?
choice_a: The converter dolly
choice_b: The first trailer, directly behind the tractor
choice_c: The last trailer in the combination
choice_d: All trailers turn over with equal likelihood
explanation: Doubles and triples are more likely to turn over than other combination vehicles because of the crack-the-whip effect, and the last trailer in a combination is most likely to turn over.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.2, Beware of the Crack-the-whip Effect

question: Why does the manual emphasize inspecting every critical part when driving doubles or triples?
choice_a: Because there are more critical parts to check when you have two or three trailers, and all of them must be checked
choice_b: Because doubles and triples do not require pre-trip inspections
choice_c: Because only the lead trailer needs inspection
choice_d: Because inspections are only legally required for single trailers
explanation: There are more critical parts to check when you have two or three trailers; the manual instructs drivers to check them all, following the procedures described in the section.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.3, Inspect Completely

question: Why must doubles and triples be driven very smoothly, looking far ahead?
choice_a: Because doubles and triples have no rearview mirrors
choice_b: It is only a fuel-efficiency recommendation
choice_c: Because braking distance is shorter than for single trailers
choice_d: To avoid rollover or jackknife, since these rigs need to slow down or change lanes gradually
explanation: Doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife; look far ahead so you can slow down or change lanes gradually when necessary.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.4, Look Far Ahead

question: Why do doubles and triples need more following distance and larger gaps than other commercial vehicles?
choice_a: They are not only longer, but also can't be turned or stopped suddenly
choice_b: Federal law sets a fixed following distance regardless of vehicle type
choice_c: They have more powerful brakes than single trailers
choice_d: They are exempt from normal following-distance guidance
explanation: Doubles and triples take up more space than other commercial vehicles; they are not only longer but also need more space because they can't be turned or stopped suddenly, so more following distance and larger gaps are needed.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.5, Manage Space

question: Why must drivers be especially careful driving double and triple bottoms in bad weather or mountain driving?
choice_a: Adverse conditions only affect single-trailer rigs
choice_b: Dead axles improve traction in bad weather
choice_c: Doubles and triples are prohibited from driving in adverse conditions
choice_d: They have greater length and more dead axles to pull with the drive axles, creating more chance for skids and loss of traction
explanation: In bad weather, slippery conditions, and mountain driving, drivers of doubles and triples must be especially careful because of greater length and more dead axles pulled by the drive axles, creating more chance for skids and loss of traction.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.6, Adverse Conditions

question: What should a driver keep in mind when parking a combination of doubles or triples?
choice_a: Parking is identical to parking a single straight truck
choice_b: Only whether the lot has painted lines
choice_c: Whether the lot has electrical hookups
choice_d: How parking lots are arranged, to avoid getting into a spot you cannot pull straight through
explanation: When parking, make sure you do not get into a spot you cannot pull straight through; be aware of how parking lots are arranged to avoid a long and difficult escape.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.7, Parking the Vehicle

question: Converter dollies built on or after what date are required to have antilock brakes?
choice_a: March 1, 1995
choice_b: March 1, 1997
choice_c: March 1, 1998
choice_d: January 1, 2000
explanation: Converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have antilock brakes; these dollies have a yellow lamp on the left side.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.1.8, Antilock Braking Systems on Converter Dollies

topic: Securing the Second Trailer Before Coupling
question: If the second (rear) trailer in a set of doubles doesn't have spring brakes, how does the driver set its emergency brakes before coupling?
choice_a: Drive the tractor close to the trailer, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, then disconnect the emergency line
choice_b: Simply chock the wheels; no air connection is needed
choice_c: Apply the trailer hand valve from the tractor cab before approaching
choice_d: Leave the trailer disconnected entirely until final hookup
explanation: If the second trailer doesn't have spring brakes, drive the tractor close to the trailer, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, and disconnect the emergency line, which sets the trailer emergency brakes if the slack adjusters are correctly adjusted.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1, Coupling Twin Trailers

question: For the safest handling on the road, which trailer should be placed in the first position behind the tractor in a set of doubles?
choice_a: The lighter trailer
choice_b: Whichever trailer was loaded first
choice_c: The more heavily loaded semitrailer
choice_d: It makes no difference to handling
explanation: For the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in the first position behind the tractor, with the lighter trailer in the rear.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1, Coupling Twin Trailers

question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A type of glad hand connector
choice_b: An electronic control unit for the ABS system
choice_c: A hydraulic jack used only for lifting trailer landing gear
choice_d: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
explanation: A converter gear (dolly) is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1, Coupling Twin Trailers

question: How does a driver release the dolly brakes before positioning the converter dolly in front of the second trailer?
choice_a: By opening the air tank petcock, or using the dolly parking brake control if the dolly has spring brakes
choice_b: The dolly brakes cannot be released manually
choice_c: By pulling the tractor's trailer air supply knob out
choice_d: By disconnecting the pintle hook entirely
explanation: Release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or if the dolly has spring brakes, use the dolly parking brake control.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1, Coupling Twin Trailers, Position Converter Dolly

topic: Connecting the Converter Dolly to the Rear Trailer
question: When backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, what should the trailer height be relative to the fifth wheel?
choice_a: Height does not matter for a converter dolly connection
choice_b: As high as possible above the fifth wheel
choice_c: Exactly level with the fifth wheel so nothing is lifted
choice_d: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
explanation: Trailer height must be correct -- slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel -- so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under it.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

topic: Connecting the Converter Dolly to the Rear Trailer
question: After connecting the converter dolly to the rear trailer and before driving, what must the driver verify at the rear of the second trailer?
choice_a: That the fuel tank is at least half full
choice_b: Nothing further is required once the pintle hook clicks
choice_c: That the tires are all the same brand
choice_d: That air pressure is present by opening the emergency line shut-off after charging trailer brakes
explanation: Charge trailer brakes (push the air supply knob in), and check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.1, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When uncoupling a converter dolly from under the rear semitrailer, why must the driver never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple
choice_b: It would only affect the electrical connector
choice_c: The pintle hook cannot physically be unlocked in that position
choice_d: It is only a cosmetic concern
explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2, Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of doubles, what should be done if the second trailer does not have spring brakes?
choice_a: Leave the wheels unchocked since the parking brake alone is sufficient
choice_b: Lower the landing gear of the first trailer instead
choice_c: Disconnect the electrical cord only
choice_d: Chock the wheels of the second trailer
explanation: As part of uncoupling the rear trailer, chock the wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes, in addition to applying parking brakes so the rig won't move.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.2, Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: What is the general method for coupling a triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: Couple the tractor to the first trailer, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the doubles coupling method
choice_b: Couple all three trailers to the tractor simultaneously
choice_c: Couple the last trailer to the tractor first, then work forward
choice_d: Triples cannot be coupled using any method described for doubles
explanation: Couple the tractor to the first trailer using the method already described for tractor-semitrailers, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.3, Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer is uncoupled first?
choice_a: All three trailers are uncoupled simultaneously
choice_b: The trailer order for uncoupling does not matter
choice_c: The third (last) trailer, by pulling the dolly out and unhitching it using the doubles uncoupling method
choice_d: The first trailer, directly behind the tractor
explanation: Uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles, before uncoupling the remainder of the rig as any double-bottom rig.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.2.3, Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: During inspection of doubles or triples, what should the driver check regarding the spare tire on the converter gear (dolly), if one is carried there?
choice_a: That the spare tire has been removed before driving
choice_b: This is not something drivers are expected to check
choice_c: That the spare tire matches the tractor's tires exactly
choice_d: That the spare tire is properly secured
explanation: If a spare tire is carried on the converter gear (dolly), the driver must make sure it's secured during the additional checks for doubles/triples.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1, Additional Checks

question: During inspection of doubles/triples, what should be checked at the pintle-eye of the dolly?
choice_a: It is not part of the required inspection
choice_b: That it is disconnected for transport
choice_c: That it is painted a specific color
choice_d: That it is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s) and that the pintle hook is latched
explanation: Be sure the pintle-eye of the dolly is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s), and make sure the pintle hook is latched.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.1, Additional Checks

question: For a set of doubles or triples, what should the shut-off valve position be at the rear of the front trailer(s)?
choice_a: It depends on the weather
choice_b: Partially open, at 50 percent
choice_c: OPEN
choice_d: CLOSED
explanation: Shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN; only the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.2, Additional Things to Check, Shut-off Valves

question: What should the position of the converter dolly air tank drain valve be during inspection?
choice_a: OPEN
choice_b: CLOSED
choice_c: It has no set required position
choice_d: Removed entirely
explanation: The converter dolly air tank drain valve should be CLOSED, along with the rear shut-off valves of the last trailer, while the shut-off valves at the rear of the front trailers should be open.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.3.2, Additional Things to Check, Shut-off Valves

question: The doubles/triples air brake check builds on the combination vehicle brake check but requires which additional checks?
choice_a: Additional air brake checks specific to double and triple trailers, such as checking that air flows to all trailers
choice_b: A check of the trailer's cargo securement only
choice_c: No additional checks are needed beyond a single trailer combination vehicle check
choice_d: Only a check of the tractor's own service brakes
explanation: Check the brakes on a double or triple trailer as you would any combination vehicle, but you must also make additional air brake checks specific to double and triple trailers.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4, Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Air Flow to All Trailers
question: For double and triple trailers, how does the driver confirm air flows all the way to the back for all the brakes to work?
choice_a: Drive the rig and observe if it stops normally
choice_b: Feel the temperature of the brake drums
choice_c: Check only the tractor's supply gauge
choice_d: Open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer and listen for air escaping, showing the entire system is charged
explanation: Push in the red trailer air supply knob to supply air to the emergency lines, then go to the rear of the rig and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer; hearing air escaping shows the entire system is charged.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Tractor Protection Valve
question: During the doubles/triples air brake check, at approximately what pressure range should the tractor protection valve control pop out or move to the emergency position?
choice_a: 100 to 125 psi
choice_b: 20 to 45 psi
choice_c: 55 to 65 psi
choice_d: 0 to 10 psi
explanation: The trailer air supply control (tractor protection valve control) should pop out, or go from "normal" to "emergency," when air pressure falls into the manufacturer-specified range, usually 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Trailer Emergency Brakes
question: What could happen if the tractor protection valve does not work properly on a doubles or triples rig?
choice_a: The vehicle would automatically shift to a lower gear
choice_b: It has no meaningful safety consequence
choice_c: An air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing the emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control
choice_d: It would only affect the trailer's turn signals
explanation: If the tractor protection valve doesn't work properly, an air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing the emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks

topic: Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check - Trailer Service Brakes
question: During the doubles/triples brake check, how does the driver test the trailer service brakes?
choice_a: There is no separate trailer service brake test for doubles/triples
choice_b: Disconnect the dolly and test each trailer separately at highway speed
choice_c: Apply only the parking brake and observe the dash light
choice_d: Move the vehicle forward slowly and apply trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve) to feel the brakes come on
explanation: Move the vehicle forward slowly and apply the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve), if so equipped; feeling the brakes come on confirms the trailer brakes are connected and working.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Subsection 7.4.1, Additional Air Brake Checks

question: According to the Kentucky manual, how many questions are on the Doubles/Triples endorsement knowledge test?
choice_a: 25 questions
choice_b: 16 questions
choice_c: 30 questions
choice_d: 20 questions
explanation: The Kentucky manual states the Doubles/Triples endorsement knowledge test consists of 20 questions, with 80 percent correct required to pass.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Testing Requirements

question: Besides Section 7, which other sections of the manual does the manual recommend studying to prepare for driving safely with double and triple trailers?
choice_a: Only Section 9, Hazardous Materials
choice_b: Sections 2, 5, and 6
choice_c: Only Section 8, Tank Vehicles
choice_d: No other sections are relevant
explanation: The manual notes that a driver preparing for the doubles/triples knowledge test should also study Sections 2, 5, and 6, which cover general driving skills, air brakes, and combination vehicles.
source_note: Kentucky Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: September 9, 2022, Kentucky-specific content revised 12/2024), Kentucky State Police / Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) Division of Driver Licensing -- Section 7, Doubles and Triples, Introduction
